scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8103: URGENT!! Both halves of Campus 2 are OFF THE NETWORK
-- nobody on the 10.5.0.x side or the 10.6.0.x side can reach their gateway
thingies (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254). This all started after "a reload" --
and OBVIOUSLY the big switch came back up without our two gateways!! It
rebooted and forgot to turn the gateway parts back on, both of them!! Please
go into the big switch, switch the two gateway things back on, and get both
floors online again!!! Thanks!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. sshswitch owns the Campus 2 L3 SVIs
  (10.5.0.254 for VLAN 5, 10.6.0.254 for VLAN 6) and they are UP. VLAN 5 hosts
  (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach 10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach
  10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / gateway outage on sshswitch that is
  not occurring (cf. kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down, where one SVI IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs
down so hosts cannot reach their gateways -- is NOT reproducible: the SVIs are up
(10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 answer), PC1 reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss, and PC3
reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the sshswitch SVIs are healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the host->gateway
paths for both VLANs, finds them working, checks the SVI state on sshswitch, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a down SVI -- restarting the switch or
blaming sshswitch's L3 interfaces to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified the “gateway parts” for both Campus 2 VLANs are up and working. The L3 gateway for 10.5.0.0/24 is on sshswitch br_v5 (10.5.0.254/24) and for 10.6.0.0/24 on sshswitch br_v6 (10.6.0.254/24). Both interfaces are UP/LOWER_UP and bound to bond0.5 and bond0.6 respectively on sshswitch. From clients on each VLAN (pc1, pc2, dc_pc5 in 10.5.0.x and pc3, pc4 in 10.6.0.x), ICMP to their gateways succeeds with 0% loss and sub-millisecond RTT. ARP resolution for both 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 returns MAC da:31:5a:0d:3e:bc, which matches sshswitch’s bond0, and arping confirms it. On the access switch side, switch4 carries VLAN 5 and 6 on the trunk (eth0.5, eth0.6) and the access ports are bridged into br_vlan5/br_vlan6, so L2 is also correct.

Mechanism: If the big switch had “forgotten” the gateways, ARP for .254 would fail or ICMP would not reply; instead, both ARP and pings are good from multiple hosts. Localization: Gateways are active on sshswitch (br_v5/br_v6 via bond0.5/bond0.6), and access VLANs on switch4 are forwarding.

Root cause: No persistent fault; the outage likely existed only during the reload boot window and recovered once sshswitch finished bringing up bond0 subinterfaces and bridges.

Corrective fix: No changes required. Gateways are already on and reachable. Recommend closing the ticket, and if users still report issues, recheck individual host configs/DHCP or transient ARP after reload; the infrastructure is healthy.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs (10.5.0.254 / 10.6.0.254) are up and answer hosts with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states sshswitch SVIs 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 are UP/LOWER_UP and respond to ICMP from hosts with 0% loss, matching the baseline-healthy note.

The agent's investigation shows repeated successful ICMP/ARP checks to 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 from multiple hosts and sshswitch's interfaces/bond0 present in the net-config output, and the writeup's claims align with those observations; the conclusion (no persistent anomaly) follows logically. Minor speculative wording about a transient reload is reasonable but not strictly proven by the logs.
